Write only the opening of this story, about 450 words in 5 to 8 paragraphs. Stop before any major revelation. Output only the story.

message.content:
The email arrived on a Tuesday, nestled amongst bills and junk mail, its subject line a jarringly bright yellow: "Northwood High - Class of '08 Reunion!" Noel almost deleted it without a second glance. Ten years. A decade. It felt both impossibly long and frighteningly short since he’d last walked those linoleum-tiled hallways, dodging rogue basketballs and the lingering scent of cafeteria mystery meat. He’d escaped Northwood, really, with a scholarship to a small liberal arts college and a fierce determination to put as much distance as possible between himself and his hometown. 

He hesitated, though. There was a small, persistent tug in his chest, a faint echo of shared memories – Friday night football games under the bleachers, the nervous excitement of prom night, the questionable fashion choices he desperately hoped had been documented and promptly buried. Mostly, he remembered the feeling of being… young. Untethered. Before the weight of adulthood settled in, before the mortgages and the responsibilities and the slow, creeping realization that life wasn’t always going to be a perfectly orchestrated soundtrack.

The email itself was predictably generic. A plea for volunteers to help organize the event, a tentative date in October, and a vaguely enthusiastic promise of “catching up and reminiscing.” It was signed by Brenda Miller, a name that sparked a fleeting, half-forgotten image of a girl with pigtails and an impressive collection of Lisa Frank stickers. He vaguely remembered she’d been fiercely organized, even back then. 

He scrolled further down, past the standard requests for contact information and suggestions for activities (bowling? karaoke? a fancy catered dinner?), until he reached the final paragraph. "We're really struggling to get things off the ground,” it read, in a slightly less enthusiastic font. “Most of the planning committee dropped out, citing… various commitments. Any help would be hugely appreciated. Even just a few hours a week would make a difference.”

Noel stared at the screen. He was, admittedly, bored. His freelance graphic design work was slow, the rain had been relentless for weeks, and his cat, Winston, was currently attempting to dismantle a throw pillow with the single-minded focus of a seasoned demolition expert. He had time. More than he realized, perhaps. 

He pictured the reunion, a chaotic gathering of familiar faces, some older, some heavier, some undoubtedly sporting questionable haircuts. He imagined awkward small talk, forced smiles, and the inevitable question of “So, what do you do now?” A wave of something that might have been mild panic washed over him. 

But then he thought of Mrs. Davison, his AP English teacher, who had instilled in him a love for stories, and Mr. Riley, the quirky history teacher who’d made the Civil War surprisingly engaging. They were probably still at Northwood. Maybe he could see them. 

With a sigh, and a completely irrational feeling of nostalgia, Noel clicked "Reply." "I'm willing to help," he typed, immediately regretting the impulsiveness. What had he just done?
